answer: In the Social (psychology) domain, original-study effect size estimates tend to be substantially larger than replication estimates: relative_es (replication/original) is lowest in Social (mean 0.278, median 0.131), effects shrink by at least half in about three-quarters of Social studies (76%), and direction reversals are most frequent there (32%). Experimental Economics shows the least original-vs-replication shrinkage (mean relative_es 0.657, median 0.698); Cognitive psychology falls in between (mean 0.509).
